about: Reference recordings of wild mallards (Anas platyrhynchos), all from xeno-canto. Licenses were checked on each recording's own page on 2026-11-13. trimStartSec/trimEndSec are seconds in the original file as downloaded. Each clip keeps at least 0.3 s before the call for the noise floor. Calls were classified by measurement against the cited call definitions in callDefinitions; uncertain clips say so in notes (and uncertain: true). Every recording used says 'Playback used: no' on its page. Mallards hybridise with domestic ducks: recordings whose page mentions a domestic, farm, captive, tame or bread-fed bird, a park, garden or city were left out; the pages of the recordings used mention none of these (wildBird). Classification is by spectrogram and measurement; no expert or recordist confirmed it.

callDefinitions.readVia: shortcut: all sources were read through web-search excerpts, because this build environment's network blocks birdsoftheworld.org, allaboutbirds.org and ducks.org (checked 2026-11-13). Quotes below are from those excerpts. Re-read the pages directly when next editing this text (owner check in docs/STATUS.md).

bow-sounds.title: Birds of the World (Cornell Lab of Ornithology), Mallard, Sounds and Vocal Behavior

du-science-calling.title: Ducks Unlimited, Understanding Waterfowl: Science and Duck Calling

du-8-calls.title: Ducks Unlimited, 8 Duck Calls Every Duck Hunter Must Master

calls.name: Hail call (hen decrescendo)
calls.definition: The female's Decrescendo Call or 'hail call', the most common call, of 2-10 notes, modal note duration 250 ms (Birds of the World). Typically five or six notes: one or two loud, forceful quacks followed by progressively shorter, softer quacks (Ducks Unlimited, Understanding Waterfowl).
calls.use: Hochbaum named it the hail call because hens appear to use it to greet ducks flying overhead (Ducks Unlimited, Understanding Waterfowl). Contagious: one calling female usually sets off other females; also elicited by the mate's slow raehb call and the sight of mallards in the air (Birds of the World).
calls.classifyBy: a series of 3-10 quacks with less than ~0.3 s between notes, the first or second note the loudest, later notes shorter and softer, the last note at least 5 dB below the loudest; isolated from other calls by >= 0.35 s.

calls.name: Hen quack (single quack)
calls.definition: The basic quack: one quack; the first call hunters should learn (Ducks Unlimited, 8 Duck Calls). The quack is the female's call; the male's most common call is a rasping rab, quieter than female quacks (Birds of the World).
calls.use: Not stated for a single quack in the excerpts read; no use is claimed here.
calls.classifyBy: one quack from a recording whose page says female, with no other mallard note within ~0.8 s before or after (so it is not part of a decrescendo series).

calls.name: Drake raeb
calls.definition: The male's most common call has a rasping rab quality and is quieter than female quacks; the slow Raehb (frequency range 1.0-4.0 kHz, modal note duration 350 ms) is one note or a series of evenly spaced notes, delivered from an alert posture with the head high (Birds of the World).
calls.use: Male mallards respond to the female's decrescendo with a slow raehb (Ducks Unlimited, Waterfowl Vocalizations); the mate's slow raehb in turn elicits the female's decrescendo (Birds of the World).
calls.classifyBy: recording page says male; rasping notes (broad, noisy spectrum rather than a clean harmonic stack) of ~0.2-0.35 s, evenly spaced, dominant frequency within 1-4 kHz.
calls.caveat: The excerpts do not separate the rab from the slow raehb clearly enough to classify clips into one or the other; the clips are evenly spaced rasping male series that fit both descriptions.

notIncluded.feed-chuckle: Ducks Unlimited (Understanding Waterfowl) describes a rapid-fire series of low-intensity sounds when ducks find good food. Only one allowed xeno-canto recording labels it (XC964309, 'female chuckle'), and there it is faint; fewer than 3 usable clips.
notIncluded.comeback-call: Described by Ducks Unlimited only as a hunter's calling pattern (fast and hard, about 5-7 notes, for ducks that do not respond); no description of a wild bird's call to classify recordings against.
notIncluded.lonesome-hen: Described by Ducks Unlimited only as a hunter's pattern (single quacks spaced out by several seconds); no separate wild call to classify against. The single hen quack is included.
notIncluded.drake-whistle: The grunt-whistle is a male courtship display call (Ducks Unlimited); not one of the hunter calls asked for; not attempted.
